items.heading: A Government Job's Stability
items.text: A government job's stability is structural, it is built into how the post itself works, independent of how well any single office or department performs. A startup job's stability is conditional, it depends on whether that specific company keeps raising money or turns profitable before it runs out of cash.

items.heading: Before the Failure and Layoff
items.text: Before the failure and layoff numbers, it helps to see the structural differences clearly, the parts that stay true regardless of which specific startup or government post you are weighing.

rows: What your job security actually depends on
Your post and your department. Termination requires proven serious misconduct, processed through a formal inquiry that can take years.
Your company's cash runway. If the startup cannot raise its next round or reach profitability before the money runs out, your role can disappear regardless of your individual performance.
A fixed 3% annual increment on basic pay, reset roughly once a decade through a pay commission.
Cash CTC negotiated per hire, often below a stable mid-size company for the same skill, offset by an equity grant whose real value depends on the company eventually reaching a liquidity event.
Not applicable in the way it applies to a company, the employer does not go out of business.
About 90% of Indian startups do not survive past five years, and a large share of the funded ones that do survive still go through at least one layoff round tied to funding cycles.
Defined by seniority and department rules; responsibility grows on a fixed, slow timeline regardless of individual capability.

Often accelerated well beyond your job title in the first 12-18 months, because small teams cannot afford to keep responsibility narrow, the upside is faster skill-building, the downside is less structured mentorship.
